clue.text: Stand erect

definitions.meaning: to stand something is to tolerate or bear it
to erect a tent or shelf is to raise and fix it in place

explanation.surface: A two-word instruction to stand upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Both tolerating a nuisance and building a structure are expressed by this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Succeed in ridding oneself of sticking plaster

definitions.meaning: to succeed at a difficult task
tearing an adhesive dressing away from the skin

explanation.surface: Someone manages to remove a stubborn plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for achieving something tricky is also the literal action of tugging a dressing away.

clue.text: From book steal binding which is hide

parts.note: to take something is to steal it
a book's binding is its cover

explanation.surface: A thief pinches the leather binding off a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From book' tells you which binding is meant: a book's cover. 'Hide' looks like leather to go with the binding, but it is a verb meaning to conceal yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelter out of sight from danger is to seek concealment, the idiom for hiding.

clue.text: Very fashionable fashion shop

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape or make it anew, so the letters are remade

explanation.surface: A smart boutique is described as very fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' is used as a verb here, rearranging the letters of SHOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart, upper-class and stylish: the adjective is a colloquial synonym for very fashionable.

clue.text: Won at cribbage, but died

definitions.meaning: in the card game cribbage players move pegs along a board, and finishing the course wins
slang for passed away

explanation.surface: A card player wins the game but drops dead at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Cribbage is a British pub card game scored by moving pegs along a holed board; the winner is the first to peg out.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing the peg-board course wins at cribbage, and the same phrase is slang for expiring.

clue.text: Noble Roman entertains idea upsetting to juvenile doctor

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: a patrician was a member of the aristocracy of ancient Rome

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning, so the letters of idea are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A Roman aristocrat hosts a notion that troubles a young doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble Roman' is the ancient Roman aristocratic class; 'upsetting' jumbles the idea, and 'entertains' seats that jumble inside the aristocrat just after his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in children's medicine is a doctor for the young, hence juvenile doctor.

clue.text: A broken nose ages

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A broken nose makes a person look older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ages' looks like a verb, but it is a plural noun meaning very long periods of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Immensely long spans of time are informally called ages.

clue.text: Yellowish earth found in loch regions

indicators.note: found in says the letters are discovered inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A yellow soil is discovered in the area around a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural clay pigment coloured by iron oxide, ranging from pale yellow to brown.

clue.text: Permit notice advertising vacancy

definitions.meaning: to permit is to allow
a sign in a window saying a property is available to rent

explanation.surface: Permission granted for a sign offering a room.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a property for rent displays a sign reading TO LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowing is expressed as 'to let', and British rental signs carry the same phrase.

clue.text: A number of Eisenhower's preferences

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
Ike was the nickname of US president Dwight Eisenhower, so Eisenhower's is Ike's

explanation.surface: Several of the president's favourite things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' here is a Roman numeral, L for fifty; 'I like Ike' was Eisenhower's campaign slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: The things you are fond of are your preferences.

clue.text: Hamlet men churn cheese

indicators.note: to churn is to stir violently, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Villagers churn out cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' suggests Shakespeare or a village, but its letters join MEN in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss hard cheese with large holes.

clue.text: Force Communist and German worker on to the dole?

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them
red is the colour of communism
und is German for and
the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker

explanation.surface: A Communist and a German labourer are forced onto unemployment benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit; the definition is cryptic, describing pushing a worker on to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying off staff whose jobs are no longer needed sends them to claim unemployment benefit.

clue.text: Part of the main Caribbean ethnic grouping from Peru

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Caribbean phrase seems to describe a Peruvian people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the open sea, an old name for the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andean people who ruled an empire centred on Cusco in what is now Peru.

clue.text: Shirt-front for Little Richard

definitions.meaning: a detachable false front worn on a shirt
a pet form of the name Richard

explanation.surface: A false shirt-front for a rock'n'roll singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachable starched bib is so called, and a diminutive of the name Dick is the same word.

clue.text: Went Socialist

definitions.meaning: went means departed
socialists are on the political ...

explanation.surface: Someone turned socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed is the past tense of leave, and the political wing of socialism has the same name.

clue.text: A profit-for the second year running?

parts.note: a profit is a gain

explanation.surface: A firm posts a profit for the second year in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: something happening a second year running happens once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating a result for another year means it happened once more.

clue.text: The city which swept Helen off her feet

definitions.meaning: a capital city

definitions.text: which swept Helen off her feet
definitions.meaning: in Greek myth the Trojan prince who carried off Helen of Sparta

explanation.surface: A city that romanced a woman named Helen.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital shares its name with the Trojan prince who abducted Helen and started the Trojan War.

clue.text: Serving meat in gravies is anathema to it

definitions.text: Serving meat in gravies is anathema to it

indicators.note: serving food means dishing it up, so the letters are dished up in a new order

explanation.surface: A diet that cannot abide meat served in sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a meat-free creed hates such dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed that forbids eating flesh would find a plate of meat and gravy abhorrent.

clue.text: One hears admission of defamation from Reykjavik resident

indicators.note: one hears says the phrase is spoken and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: someone confessing to defaming others would say 'I slander'

explanation.surface: A Reykjavik man confesses to libel.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, 'I slander' is how the answer is pronounced; Reykjavik is the capital of Iceland.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the capital of that Nordic island is a citizen of the country.

clue.text: Counterfeit way to become rich

definitions.meaning: to counterfeit is to forge banknotes
a phrase for earning a fortune

explanation.surface: Forgery as a get-rich-quick scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Printing forged cash literally manufactures currency, and the same phrase means getting wealthy.

clue.text: Vintage which is proof against attack?

definitions.text: Vintage which is proof against attack?

parts.words: Vintage which is proof against attack?
parts.note: a drink strengthened like a castle against assault, playing on alcoholic proof and on defensive works

explanation.surface: A wine strong enough to withstand a siege.
explanation.walkthrough: A wine strengthened with added spirit, such as port or sherry, is described as if its walls were built up against attack; 'proof' also nods to alcoholic strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Port and sherry are wines strengthened with spirit, described as if defended like a fort.

clue.text: Dig out some food

definitions.meaning: to dig up or root out
slang for food

explanation.surface: Excavate something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooting in the soil is grubbing, and slang for something to eat is the same word.

clue.text: Gambled after losing a returned pound

indicators.note: after losing says letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: the clue's first word taken as written

indicators.note: returned means the abbreviation is turned back to front

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone bet and then lost a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter reuses the definition word as the wordplay's base: a pound weight is abbreviated with two letters, and 'returned' turns them round before 'after losing' takes them out.
explanation.definitionFit: To game is to play for stakes, so gamed is a synonym of bet.

clue.text: Like lamp until switched

indicators.note: switched means changed around, so the letters are swapped

explanation.surface: A lamp remains dark until switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a lamp is dark until someone switches it on.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp not yet switched on gives no light.

clue.text: Rex leaves friend to the devil

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the letter goes out of the word

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A king abandons his friend to Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex is Latin for king, abbreviated R.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon or evil spirit is a devil.

clue.text: Chum has minute tropical tree

parts.note: a chum is a friend or pal

explanation.surface: A friend owns a tiny tropical tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' wants to mean tiny, but it is the unit of time, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: Coconut and date trees are examples of this tropical family.

clue.text: Looker-on or an onlooker?

definitions.meaning: one who looks on, into the future
one who sees, a watcher

explanation.surface: A spectator or a bystander.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet looks forward into the future, and literally someone who sees is a watcher.

clue.text: Knockout staff with firm call for silence

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
sh is said to ask for quiet

explanation.surface: Stunning employees with a firm order to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but means a stick; a cosh is a British word for a cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: A short heavy club used to knock someone unconscious.

clue.text: One beset by all men in confusion for thousands of years

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on all sides, so this letter goes inside
confusion means disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A lone figure surrounded by a confused crowd of men across the ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the anagram fodder, not a link: ALL MEN IN is jumbled, and 'beset by' puts I among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Periods of a thousand years each, plural of millennium.

clue.text: Look back to study of ancient times

indicators.note: back says the word for look is turned round

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
a den is a private room, a study

explanation.surface: Glancing back toward a study of antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LO into OL; 'study' is the room, not research.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to times long past, an old-fashioned word for former days.

clue.text: Tell man not to use washing powder

parts.note: with 'not to use', tell means discourage, as in to deter
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: An instruction to a man not to use soap powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell ... not to use' together means discourage, though the check can only hold 'Tell'; 'man' is the polite British word for a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleansing agent sold as powder or liquid for laundry.

clue.text: Hound the third in line for the throne

definitions.meaning: to hound is to pester or harass

definitions.text: the third in line for the throne
definitions.meaning: Prince ... was third in line to the British throne when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: Persecuting a junior royal.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass is to hound, and Prince Harry was once third in the British line of succession.
